hook.text: You run a marathon on a hot day. Your body keeps its core temperature at 37 degrees despite massive external stress.

buildup.text: Homeostasis is a system's tendency to maintain internal stability despite external changes.

discovery.text: Walter Cannon named the concept in the 1920s.

twist.text: Organizations have homeostasis too. Culture resists change. Processes resist reform.

climax.text: To change a homeostatic system, you need sustained pressure. Brief pushes get absorbed.

punchline.text: Systems fight to stay the same. Only persistence shifts them.

quiz.question: Why does homeostasis make organizational change difficult?
options: Culture and processes resist deviation and absorb brief change efforts
